question: Who wrote 'An Era of Darkness: The British Empire in India'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shashi Tharoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shashi Tharoor**, a renowned Indian author, politician, and diplomat, wrote the book **'An Era of Darkness: The British Empire in India'**.
 
• The book was published in **2016** and critiques the exploitative practices of British colonial rule in India.
 
• In this work, Tharoor elaborates on the economic, cultural, and social damages caused by the British Empire during its rule in India, often using historical evidence and statistics.
 
• The book is based on Tharoor’s famous speech at the **Oxford Union debate in 2015**, where he argued for reparations for colonial damages caused by Britain.
 
• 'An Era of Darkness' is lauded for its detailed and compelling narrative, exposing the harsh realities of colonial exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vikram Seth**

 
 
• Vikram Seth is an acclaimed Indian author and poet, best known for his novel **'A Suitable Boy'**, which is one of the longest novels ever published in English.
 
• Seth’s works often explore themes of love, relationships, and the intricacies of Indian society.
 
• His other notable works include **'The Golden Gate'**, a novel in verse, and **'An Equal Music'**, which focuses on the life of a violinist.
 
 
 
• **Pavan K. Varma**
 
 
• Pavan K. Varma is an Indian diplomat and author known for his works on Indian culture and society.
 
• His notable books include **'The Great Indian Middle Class'** and **'Being Indian'**, which provide deep insights into Indian identity and its evolution.
 
• Varma often delves into topics related to India’s socio-political framework and cultural ethos.
 
 
 
• **Romila Thapar**
 
 
• Romila Thapar is a prominent Indian historian, well-known for her scholarly works on ancient Indian history.
 
• Her major works include **'A History of India'** and **'Ashoka and the Decline of the Mauryas'**.
 
• Thapar has extensively written about the cultural, political, and social aspects of ancient India, providing a nuanced perspective on historical events.
